settle: More exposed days (the 2021-22 and later files are not on the portal by school day), school-level data with air-conditioning status, or absence by reason. An endpoint with a standard error near 0.001 would be needed to test the composed size.

notes:
Model as registered; 2158 school days from 2006-09-05 to 2019-06-26 after excluding 218 days with low citywide enrolment (mostly Regents examination weeks in late January and June) and 9 days with absence above 30%. Mean absence rate 8.8%. Secondary estimates, none deciding: {"lag0_2": {"ratio": 1.0128, "lo": 0.9812, "hi": 1.0455, "n": 601}, "per_5C": {"ratio": 0.9909, "lo": 0.9795, "hi": 1.0025, "n": 601}, "without_last_two_weeks_of_June": {"ratio": 1.0068, "lo": 0.973, "hi": 1.0417, "n": 578}}. Influenza is not controlled, and in the cold arm it is the main rival. The test was registered knowing it could not detect the composed size (D below 4).

After the referee (13 Nov 2026): the referee reproduced the estimate (1.009, 0.970 to 1.050) and no variant moves it away from 1. A placebo exposure, TMAX at or above 30 C two days later with today's exposure in the model, gives 1.021 (0.985 to 1.058), as large as the estimate itself, so the small positive point estimate reflects the end-of-year decline in attendance and not the day's heat; it comes from May and June (September alone 0.995). Rule 8 gives the same verdict as rule 2: D = 0.1. The stance is now the endpoint stance of rules 7 and 8 (0.04), as for the cold arm. A citywide rate cannot show an effect confined to schools without air conditioning, and air-conditioning status by school and year is not in the open files. The published relative risk (PMID 27343213) concerns all ages in Hong Kong, where adults were the most sensitive and children under 5 the least.

stance.note: Rules 7 and 8: agreement of the endpoint with the composed prediction, scaled by how well the test separates the chain from no effect. The earlier value was the stance of a direct effect against its null.
